# Incident Report — 2021-09-10 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim Host

| Field | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | **10.9.10.102** | Sole active LAN endpoint driving all outbound activity; DHCP client (frames 1–4) |
| MAC | **00:4f:49:b1:e8:c3** | ARP: "Who has 10.9.10.9? Tell 10.9.10.102" (frame 14) is answered as coming from this MAC; same MAC registers all NBNS names for this host |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-KKITB6Q** | DHCP option 12 hostname; NBNS registration `DESKTOP-KKITB6Q<00>/<20>`; DNS PTR-style queries `DESKTOP-KKITB6Q.angrypoutine.com` |
| Logged-in user | **hobart.gunnarsson** | Kerberos AS-REQ `CNameString = hobart.gunnarsson` from 10.9.10.102 to DC 10.9.10.9 |
| AD domain / DC | angrypoutine.com / **ANGRYPOUTINE-DC** at 10.9.10.9 | LDAP/Kerberos/DCERPC/SMB2 traffic to 10.9.10.9; DNS SRV query `_ldap._tcp.Default-First-Site-Name._sites.dc._msdcs.angrypoutine.com` resolving to 10.9.10.9 |

LAN is 10.9.10.0/24; 10.9.10.9 is both DHCP server and domain controller.

## What happened

At **T+139.5s**, 10.9.10.102 resolved `simpsonsavingss.com` to **194.62.42.206** and issued a direct `GET /bmdff/BhoHsCtZ/MLdmpfjaX/5uFG3Dz7yt/date1?BNLv65=pAAS` (four random path segments, two-letter query key — no referrer, no preceding page load captured in this pcap). The request used a spoofed legacy user agent (`Mozilla/4.0 ... MSIE 7.0 ... Trident/7.0`), consistent with a non-browser downloader/stager rather than an actual user click. The server (Apache/2.4.6 CentOS, PHP/7.2.34) returned **HTTP 200** with `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="date6"` and a 284,816-byte **PE32+ x86-64 DLL** payload (confirmed via `--export-objects http` and `file`). The DLL exports `DllRegisterServer`/`DllUnregisterServer` (regsvr32-loadable), imports only a handful of `kernel32.dll` functions (`VirtualAlloc`, `VirtualFree`, `LoadLibraryA`, `GetProcAddress`, `CreateThread`, `WaitForMultipleObjects`), and contains large obfuscated string blobs — the signature of a minimal shellcode-staging loader rather than a full-featured payload.

**4.5 seconds later (T+144.06s)**, 10.9.10.102 opened a TLS 1.2 connection directly to IP **167.172.37.9:443** with **no SNI extension** (never resolved via DNS). The server presented a **self-signed certificate**, CN=`londonareloeli.uk`, O=`LL EST`, OU=`UK System`, L=`London`, C=`UK`, issued 2021-09-08.

From **T+148.7s through the end of the capture (T+4512s, ~76 minutes)**, the host repeatedly re-connected over TLS 1.2 to **94.158.245.52:443**, again always with no SNI, roughly every 3–8 minutes for the full remaining capture duration — a classic C2 beacon cadence. This session presented the **identical self-signed certificate** (CN=`londonareloeli.uk`) as the 167.172.37.9 connection, confirming both IPs are the same C2 infrastructure.

All other traffic (Windows Update `.cab`/`.exe` downloads from Akamai-hosted `*.windowsupdate.com`, Microsoft Store image fetches, Office/Teams/OneDrive telemetry, NCSI connectivity checks, single unconfirmed queries to `gameplayapi.intel.com` and `myexternalip.com`) is legitimate Windows/Microsoft background activity and does not correlate with the infection timeline.

## Malware family

**Attribution confidence: behavioral (not signature-confirmed).** No IDS/Suricata alert export was provided alongside this pcap, so there is no signature-based confirmation available.

Behavioral fingerprint: HTTP-delivered DLL payload retrieved via an obfuscated multi-segment random URI with a spoofed legacy-IE user agent, `regsvr32`-loadable export set (`DllRegisterServer`), minimal-import shellcode-staging loader, and near-immediate pivot to a TLS/443 C2 channel using self-signed certificates reused across multiple bare-IP endpoints (no SNI). This constellation of traits is most consistent with a **Zloader-style DLL loader/downloader**. Treat the family name as a working hypothesis pending sandbox detonation or signature confirmation, not a confirmed identification.

## Indicators of Compromise
